- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment spikes sharply (e.g., +1.00) followed by a drop, model often overshoots and then undercorrects — cap peak forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- High news volume (≥3) with low sentiment change suggests market noise; model should not overreact — dampen forecast volatility.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, check for sentiment lag — if sentiment is flat or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to adjust — apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–5 days post-peak.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is low, model tends to underestimate — add 1–3% upward bias to compensate.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility — if sentiment is neutral or declining, apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast amplitude.
